newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-UK JUDGE TO REEXAMINE HILLSBOROUGH DEATHS EVIDENCE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-UK JUDGE TO REEXAMINE HILLSBOROUGH DEATHS EVIDENCE.

text.p: The British government said on Monday a top judge would to investigate if there were grounds to reopen an inquiry into the 1989 Hillsborough tragedy, when 96 fans were crushed to death at a soccer match.
The announcement by Home Secretary Jack Straw delighted families of the victims, who have campaigned for greater compensation and for police conduct at the disaster to be re-examined.
Straw told parliament he had asked Lord Justice Stuart Smith to examine if there was new video and medical evidence to warrant a further public inquiry.

A television documentary last December claimed to have found new evidence about the disaster, which happened at a cup semi-final match between Nottingham Forest and Liverpool at the Hillsborough stadium in Sheffield, northern England.

"I am determined to go as far as I can to ensure that no matter of significance is overlooked and that we do not reach a final conclusion without a full and independent examination of the evidence," Straw said.
His Conservative predecessor at the Home Office said he would not reopen the inquiry unless he was convinced it would be in the public interest.

Straw, of the Labour party which won elections two months ago, said: "We owe it to everyone touched by the tragedy, but above all to the families of those who died, to get to the bottom of this matter once and for all."
He said he hoped the judge could report by December 31. If the judge found that any evidence had been overlooked during three previous inquiries, he said, he would take whatever action was necessary.
Many relatives of the victims -- all Liverpool fans -- travelled to London to hear Straw's statement and to meet him.

Trevor Hicks, a spokesman for the group, said they were very pleased with the outcome. "He has given us what we had asked for -- the opportunity to put before (the judge) what we believe is damning evidence," he said.
